from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cross product calculates area spanned by two vectors.",
            "The determinant finds this area as signed quantity.",
            "Positive area means counter-clockwise rotation, negative is clockwise."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: Orientation and Determinants", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements
        axes = Axes(x_length=3, y_length=3, axis_config={"include_tip": True}).add_coordinates()
        vec_a = Vector([1, 2], color=YELLOW)
        vec_b = Vector([2, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        parallelogram = Polygon([0,0,0], [1,2,0], [3,2.5,0], [2,0.5,0], fill_opacity=0.3, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b))
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        det_text = MathTex(r"\det = ad - bc").set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(det_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We represent this operation using a 3x3 matrix.",
            "Place basis vectors i, j, k at the top.",
            "Determinant expansion computes the resulting vector components.",
            "Remember the anti-commutative property: A x B = -B x A.",
            "Example: i x j gives the unit vector k."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Determinant Formula for 3D", lecture_lines)
        
        # 3x3 Matrix for Cross Product
        matrix = MathTex(
            "\\begin{pmatrix} \\mathbf{i} & \\mathbf{j} & \\mathbf{k} \\\\ a_1 & a_2 & a_3 \\\\ b_1 & b_2 & b_3 \\end{pmatrix}",
            font_size=40
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        i_box = SurroundingRectangle(matrix[0][0:3], color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(i_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        formula = MathTex("\\mathbf{i}(a_2b_3 - a_3b_2) - \\mathbf{j}(a_1b_3 - a_3b_1) + \\mathbf{k}(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1)", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(matrix.copy(), formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        prop = MathTex("\\mathbf{a} \\times \\mathbf{b} = -(\\mathbf{b} \\times \\mathbf{a})", font_size=36, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(prop, 'D5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(prop))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        ex = MathTex("\\mathbf{i} \\times \\mathbf{j} = \\mathbf{k}", font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(ex, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(ex))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Meaning and Physical Applications", [
            "Magnitude of cross product equals |A||B|sin(theta).",
            "Torque is the physical application of this concept.",
            "Torque equals the radius vector times force vector."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, RIGHT*2 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*2.5 + UP*1.5, RIGHT*0.5 + UP*1.0,
            color="#FF8000"
        )
        fill = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, RIGHT*2 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*2.5 + UP*1.5, RIGHT*0.5 + UP*1.0,
            fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#808080", stroke_width=0
        )
        group = VGroup(fill, parallelogram)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'A2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF8000"))
        self.play(Create(parallelogram), FadeIn(fill))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.play(group.animate.scale(1.2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(group))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Quick Check", [
            "Cross product result is always a vector.",
            "Dot product result is always a scalar value.",
            "Changing vector order reverses the resulting vector direction."
        ])
        
        # Elements to display
        vec_icon = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=BLUE)
        scalar_icon = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.2)
        reverse_icon = VGroup(
            Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=RED),
            Arrow(start=RIGHT, end=LEFT, color=RED)
        ).arrange(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_icon, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_icon), Flash(vec_icon, color=BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_icon, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(scalar_icon), Flash(scalar_icon, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(reverse_icon, 'D2')
        self.play(FadeIn(reverse_icon), Flash(reverse_icon, color=RED))
        self.wait(1)

        # Final checkmark
        checkmark = Checkmark().set_color(GREEN).scale(2) if "Checkmark" in globals() else Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color=GREEN).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, 'E4')
        self.play(Create(checkmark))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Cross Product: From 2D Geometry to 3D Space

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Orientation and Determinants
sections.content: Briefly introduce the 2D 'Signed Area' concept. Explain that for two vectors, the cross product relates to the area of the parallelogram they span. Use the determinant notation |a b; c d| = ad - bc as the foundational tool.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D robot arm: The 'signed area' tells us if the arm is turning clockwise (negative) or counter-clockwise (positive).

sections.title: The 3D Cross Product: Definition and Right-Hand Rule
sections.content: Transition to 3D space. Define the cross product (a × b) as a vector perpendicular to both input vectors. Introduce the Right-Hand Rule: fingers curl from a to b, thumb points in the direction of the result vector.
sections.example: An animator setting the axis of rotation for a digital character's shoulder; the cross product helps define the normal vector for the rotation plane.

sections.title: The Determinant Formula for 3D
sections.content: Show the formal calculation using the unit vectors i, j, k in the top row of a 3x3 matrix. Emphasize that the cross product is distributive and anti-commutative (a × b = -(b × a)).
sections.example: Calculating the cross product of vector A=(1,0,0) and B=(0,1,0) to yield vector K=(0,0,1).

sections.title: Geometric Meaning and Physical Applications
sections.content: Explain that the magnitude |a × b| = |a||b|sin(θ). Relate this to physical torque: Torque = radius vector × force vector.
sections.example: A squirrel pushing a door: The cross product explains why pushing perpendicular to the door (max sin 90°) creates the most torque compared to pushing at an angle.

sections.title: Summary and Quick Check
sections.content: Review key takeaways: Result is a vector, magnitude is area, direction is normal. Ensure students distinguish between Dot Product (scalar) and Cross Product (vector).
sections.example: Interactive poll: If you swap the order of the vectors, how does the resulting vector change? (Correct answer: It points in the opposite direction).
